item.title: Spain train crash: US, Japan and Canada citizens among dead, authorities say
item.description:
The train disaster, one of Europe’s deadliest rail incidents this century, killed 69 people, including 54 Spaniards Four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed in last week’s high-speed train collision in Spain, authorities said. Wednesday’s disaster – one of Europe’s deadliest rail accidents this century – has seen victims’ relatives endure an agonising wait as forensics teams identify the dead, sometimes from individual body parts. item.title: Sir Patrick Stewart, RIP
item.description:
Patrick Stewart, as Captain Jean-Luc Picard. (CBS) The great British actor Sir Patrick Stewart passed away on Thursday . While Stewart began his career as a stage actor and performed in many Shakespeare plays, he is best known for his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, in Star Trek: The Next Generation . Thanks to his impressive performance, Stewart and the character he played became science fiction icons. Stewart brought extraordinary depth and perception to the role. And the character is an interesting contrast to the more instinctive and aggressive, less cerebral, Captain Kirk in the original Star Trek Series . Perhaps more than any other character, Stewart's Picard epitomized Star Trek's progressive liberal values: Enlightenment rationalism, technological optimism (highlighted by his defense of the rights of the android Data ), racial and ethnic equality, and commitment to peace…

item.title: Trump’s List of Alleged Noncitizen Voters in California May Be Filled With Errors
item.description:
The Trump administration’s bid to stop 20,000 “likely noncitizen” voters from casting midterm ballots in California appears to be based on a list that’s riddled with inaccuracies. Two data analysts at the University of California, Los Angeles’ Voting Rights Project found that over 40 percent of the people the Department of Justice has deemed likely noncitizens were not even on the state’s voter rolls in the first place, and many others are likely legally eligible to vote. The analysts shared the conclusion in a legal filing on Saturday . The Justice Department’s list was shared the day before as a result of the Voting Rights Project’s lawsuit with the Los Angeles-based Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) against the Trump administration’s attempts to interfere in the election. item.title: UN warns of security risks in Western Sahara as peacekeeping mission ends
item.description:
The 35-year-old UN peacekeeping mission ⁠in the disputed Western Sahara region came to an end Sunday after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate. Morocco, which claims the region as its own, welcomed the decision, while its opponents from the Algeria-backed Polisario Front called it "unacceptable".
